desc:
The array nums has an even length and contains exactly as many positive numbers as negative numbers (there are no zeros). Rearrange it so that:

  • positive and negative numbers alternate, starting with a positive number (positives at even indices, negatives at odd indices), and
  • the positives keep their original relative order, and so do the negatives.

Return the rearranged array. For example, [3, 1, -2, -5, 2, -4] becomes [3, -2, 1, -5, 2, -4].
hints: The result is fully determined: slot 0 gets the first positive, slot 1 the first negative, slot 2 the second positive, and so on.
Splitting into two lists and interleaving works in O(n) but with extra lists. Can you write each element straight to its final position?
Keep two write pointers: pos = 0 stepping by 2 for positives and neg = 1 stepping by 2 for negatives. Scan the input once and place every element at the pointer of its sign.
editorial: Since the counts of positives and negatives are equal and the order inside each group must be preserved, the k-th positive must land at index 2k and the k-th negative at index 2k + 1. Scanning the input once with two independent write pointers, one for even and one for odd output slots, produces exactly that.

This is a stable partition into an output array. Doing it truly in place while keeping both orders is much harder (it needs rotations and costs O(n<sup>2</sup>) or fancier merge tricks), which is why the problem is normally solved with an output array of size n.
